jobs.description:
Job Description

This position has been deemed critical by the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring pause.

This position is based on Stanford’s main campus with consideration given to the option for a hybrid work schedule (partially onsite 3 or more days a week), subject to operational need.

Interested candidates must include a resume and cover letter to be considered for this position.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa.

About Us

The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school is made up of a three-part structure to drive global impact: Our academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people; Institutes bridge scholarship at Stanford and beyond, bringing multiple viewpoints to bear on urgent challenges; The Sustainability Accelerator drives new policy and technology solutions through a worldwide network of partners who work with our teams to develop solutions at a global scale. The school is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change.

For more information on the school, click here .

Precourt Institute for Energy

As part of the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability , the Precourt Institute for Energy concentrates the talents of the University on energy research and education, from basic science and technology to policy and business. We disseminate research results and help the University develop energy-literate leaders as part of its educational mission. We work across campus in all seven of Stanford’s schools. We also build collaborations globally with industry, other research institutions, government, and civic organizations in pursuit of sustainable, affordable, secure energy for all people.

Seeking Managing Director, Stanford Center for Sustainability in Southeast Asia:

Seeking exceptional candidates to serve as the Managing Director of the Stanford Center for Sustainabilit in Southeast Asia, a high-impact new research center within the Precourt Institute aimed at developing and implementing long term, holistic solutions for the sustainability of Southeast Asian communities and the envionments on which they depend.

Working in conjunction with the Stanford Center for Sustainability in Southeast Asia faculty Director and reporting directly to the Precourt Institute Director, the Managing Director will lead the development, management, and execution of the Center for Sustainability in Southeast Asia (CSSA). The Managing Director will create, direct, and lead the implmentation of innovative programs, parthnerships, and projects across Southeast Asia that leverage the broad and deep expertise of Stanford faculty and students and partner them with local organizations in academia, government, business, and civil society to create long-term value and transformative impact for achieving sustainability of Southeast Asian communities at risk due to the effecs of climate change, extreme weather, environmental degradaition, ocean warming, unregulated evelopment, and other factors. The Managing Director will also have a leading role in business development for the Center, encompassing building and maintaining a national, regional, and global network of individual, governmental, and corporate donors. These activities will require the ability to represent the Center at high-level business development meetings, interfacing with leaders in Southeast Asia and beyond. The position requires leadership, self-direction, and initiative to further build and strengthen CSSA within Stanford and externally with existing and new partner institutions and collaborators in Southeast Asia and globally.

The Stanford Center For Sustainability In Southeast Asia

The Stanford Center for Sustainability in Southeast Asia (CSSA) is a new holistic and integrated center that brings together faculty and researchers from all across the Stanford community to work hand-in-hand with key partners and stakeholders from across Southeast Asia and globally. The mission of the Stanford CSSA is to conduct research and analysis, develop strategic partnerships, and implement innovative solutions in three main research pillars: (1) Energy transition and the digital transformation of society; (2) Sustainability of coastal and terrestial communities at risk, including food and water security, climate adaptation, disaster resilence, and degradation of ocean ecosystems. (3) Governance at the global, regional, national, and local levels.

CSSA builds upon many years of engagement across Soitheast Asia by Stanford faculty, researchers, and partner centers. Located in the Doerr School it draws upon the School’s expertise in environmental, energy, and innovation leadership. CSSA ’s mission is also to reacg beyond the Doerr School to mobilize faculty across the Stanford campus, connect them with counterpart institutions and researchers in Southeast Asia in order to implement significant integrated innovation across its core areas.

Significant and Diverse Experience and Expertise in environmental sustainability in more than one Southeast Asian country and globally. Significant experience, knowledge, and network in multiple dimensions of sustainability, at the global, national, and local levels. ideally including marine environments, coastal community resilience, deforestation, food security, carbon politics, environmental impacts, regulatory and legal frameworks, economics, and policy implications. Strong candidates will have experience with and understanding of scientici innovation, emerging solutions in sustainability fo Southeast Asian communties and societies, and the capacity to analyze the viability of such solutions in the changing global and regional economic, social, and political contexts. Strong candidates will be expected to have > 10 years of experience in these areas.

Strong Organizational and Management Experience and Skills: Significant experience and track record of success in leading and managing complex, multi-disciplinary organizations and teams is desired, along with excellent communication skills.

Job Description

Position Description

The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships serves as a key member of the Library’s executive leadership team and works collaboratively with leadership to plan, design, implement, and evaluate all facets of programs and partnerships. The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships oversees system wide programming, exhibitions, and outreach for youth, families, adults, older adults, and seniors, as well as programs and services offered through The Bridge at Main – Literacy & Learning Center. The role also includes oversight of Mobile Outreach Services (MOS), which operates a fleet of four bookmobiles, and the Jail and Reentry Services (JARS) unit serving the County Jails.

Role Description

Reporting to the City Librarian and under the supervision of the Chief of Public Services, the Chief of Community Programs & Partnerships is a member of the Public Services Team and works collaboratively with the Main Library Manager, the Chief of Branches, the Chief of Collections & Technical Services, and the City Archivist. The Chief of Community Programs & Partnerships also works collaboratively with the other divisions chiefs on the executive leadership team who oversee support divisions (Facilities, Finance, Information Technology, and Research, Strategy & Analytics).

The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships collaborates closely with other City departments such as SF Recreation & Parks Department, SF Arts Commission, SFMTA, Office of Economic & Workforce Development, and the Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector. The role also partners with libraries regionally, statewide, and nationally.

The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships supports key initiatives of the Mayor’s Office, such as the SF Poet Laureate, SF Drag Laureate, and SF Youth Poet Laureate, and leads the Library’s signature programs, including One City One Book: SF Reads and Summer Stride .

As the Library’s liaison to the Friends & Foundation of the San Francisco Public Library, the Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships cultivates relationships and strengthens partnerships with community‑based organizations, nonprofits, and other civic partners.

The Community Programs and Partnerships (CPP) Division is designed to oversee and coordinate diverse teams that focus on all aspects of youth engagement including early childhood services, teen services and services to schools. The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships is responsible for leading teams that collaborate with the Chief of Branches, Chief of Main, and City Archivist to strengthen neighborhood services through community programs, outreach, and exhibitions. They support the area of instruction and learning, including innovative approaches to provide e-learning, instruction and trans-literacy services will be a key aspect in leading the division.

The Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships oversees a wide range of teams to produce an array of services meeting the needs of 21st Century learners. Under the Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships, the teams will challenge conventional approaches to library services by focusing on creative approaches to partnerships that leverage resources, talent and technology. The incumbent will take a lead role in establishing and sustaining strong relationships with government, education, corporate and non-profit entities in an effort to make the library a key partner in the civic life of San Francisco residents. Through these partnerships, the SFPL will serve a diverse and active community that will take full opportunity to access services and programs at all 28 neighborhood libraries and other agencies. The Chief will formulate and assist in the development of division and departmental budget; direct and coordinate policy development; provide direction and leadership in developing a systemwide public programs and outreach efforts; assess and respond to community needs; and perform other job related duties as assigned.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate for the Chief of Community Programs and Partnerships is a strategic, collaborative, and community‑focused leader who excels at building partnerships, directing innovative public programs, and advancing inclusive services for diverse learners. They bring strong leadership, political acumen, and exceptional communication skills to guide systemwide programming, outreach, exhibitions, and youth engagement initiatives. This individual thrives in fast‑paced, complex environments and ensures SFPL remains a key civic partner in San Francisco. Excellent communication, public speaking, and presentation skills are essential.

Job Description

This position has been deemed critical by the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring pause.

This is a three-year fixed-term position, with the possibility of renewal dependent on programmatic need and budgetary availability.

This position is based on Stanford’s main campus with consideration given to the option for a hybrid work schedule (partially onsite and offsite), subject to operational need. Interested candidates must include a resume and cover letter to be considered for this position.

About Us

The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school is made up of a three-part structure to drive global impact: Our academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people; Institutes bridge scholarship at Stanford and beyond, bringing multiple viewpoints to bear on urgent challenges; The Sustainability Accelerator drives new policy and technology solutions through a worldwide network of partners who work with our teams to develop solutions at a global scale. The school is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change.

For more information on the school, click here .

Precourt Institute for Energy

As part of the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability
, the Precourt Institute for Energy
concentrates the talents of the University on energy research and education, from basic science and technology to policy and business. Our mission is to spark the creativity, collaboration, learning, and leadership needed for the global energy transformation. The initiatives, research centers, and educational programs of the Precourt Institute connect across campus in all seven of Stanford’s schools supporting work with the potential to solve the toughest energy challenges from science and engineering to policy and economics. We also build collaborations globally with industry, other research institutions, government, and civic organizations in pursuit of sustainable, affordable, secure energy for all people.

STEER

STEER is an initiative joint between Stanford’s Precourt Institute for Energy and the SLAC National Laboratory. Operating at the intersection of engineering, economics, and innovation, STEER is focused on overcoming technological uncertainties to guide strategic deployment of capital and scaling of solutions.

Senior Academic Staff Researcher

The Precourt Institute is seeking a Senior Academic Staff Researcher to serve as the managing director and leader of STEER, providing strategic leadership and direction of complex scientific, engineering, and technical research with responsibility for overall success. Working with the faculty council, the Senior Academic Staff Researcher/managing director oversees a multi-million-dollar diversified funding portfolio (government, industry and philanthropy) and a multidisciplinary team of scholars, practitioners, faculty, postdocs, and students.

Key Responsibilities

In partnership with the STEER faculty council:

Develop and execute frontier research strategies to advance STEER's vision of guiding "what to build, where to innovate, and how to invest" — with a focus on directing public, private, and philanthropic capital toward the efficient scaling of energy and sustainability solutions.
Engage external stakeholders — including industry practitioners, policymakers, and investors — to understand their decision-making needs and translate Stanford's strategic analyses into actionable insights.
Build and sustain strong partnerships across Stanford, including with other units, faculty, and trainees.
Develop and oversee research questions and hypotheses, work plans, and operational processes, and work with faculty, researchers, and staff to deliver high-quality analyses, research outputs, and programmatic milestones on time and within scope.
Develop policies and procedures as they relate to academic or research activities.
Oversee the day-to-day operations of STEER as a multi-PI research collaborative. For example, overseeing internal coordination and communication, graduate fellow, postdoc and staff hiring.
Raise funds from government, industry, and foundations to support STEER's growth, and steward productive and lasting relationships with funders.
Ensure successful execution of funded programs by monitoring progress, managing risks, and maintaining accountability for meeting sponsor expectations and contractual commitments.
Manage staff, which includes recruiting, hiring, developing, evaluating, and setting priorities; manage business, technical, and educational activities for direct reports including managers and technical experts

API Legal Outreach is the largest social justice legal organization focused on the Asian/Pacific Islander, Latinx, and immigrant communities of the Greater Bay Area and the Central Valley. With offices in Oakland and San Francisco, our work is focused in the areas of Gender-based Violence, Immigration and Immigrant Rights, Disability Rights, Senior Law and Elder Abuse, Anti-Human Trafficking, Youth Violence Prevention, Anti API Hate Violence, the preservation of affordable housing and small businesses, and other social justice issues.

What’s the job and who is Nuru?

Nuru is seeking a multidisciplinary professional with a demonstrated systems thinking, strategic writing, and project management background in international development and impact investing to serve as our Development Systems & Grants Director. This is an internal-facing project management role intentionally designed for a tech-driven operator who thrives on transforming data, donor intelligence, and programmatic knowledge into compelling narratives, strategic insights, and funding opportunities. This is not a lead generation or donor relationship cultivation role. Rather, the Director serves as the architect of Nuru's private and corporate internal fundraising systems, knowledge management processes, and proposal pipeline - we call this “running the internal fundraising machine”. Working closely with the Chief Sustainability Officer, Senior Leadership Team, and a part-time Salesforce Administrator, this role ensures that organizational knowledge is transformed into high-quality proposals, reports, donor profiles, and strategic decision-making tools. The ideal candidate combines deep sectoral expertise with exceptional writing and analytical abilities and possesses a demonstrated track record of designing, managing, and implementing programs that improve rural livelihoods and economic empowerment in geographies relevant to Nuru's mission and vision.

Nuru is a U.S. 501(c)(3) nonprofit with the ability to hire employees globally. Founded in 2008, Nuru is a global collective of locally-led NGO’s working to break cycles of unjust poverty in marginalized communities across the Nuru Collective. We achieve this by helping smallholder farmers transition from subsistence to professionalized farming. While Nuru staff work across separate and locally led organizations in different countries, we are united by a shared vision to expand meaningful choices for the communities we serve. 

A pioneer in remote work, Nuru has been fully remote since 2008. Our team members work from the locations that suit them best, and we remain committed to this flexible, remote-first model. For this role, candidates must be able to maintain regular working overlap with the U.S. Eastern Time.

What you’ll be doing:

● Systems Architecture & Development Operations 

Serve as the architect of Nuru's private and corporate fundraising systems, transforming donor intelligence and organizational knowledge into actionable insights for leadership.
Supervise and prioritize the work of the Salesforce Administrator to ensure Salesforce remains the organization's trusted source of truth.
Design and maintain proposal pipelines, donor profiles, strategic brief sheets, and knowledge management systems that support fundraising effectiveness.
Oversee data governance standards and oversee CRM processes, reporting structures, and operational workflows.
Collaborate closely with the Chief Implementation Officer and Business Development Director to ensure alignment across public and private fundraising efforts.

● Institutional Grants & Lifecycle Strategy

Lead the writing, editing, and collaborative execution of high-quality grant proposals, concept notes, and letters of intent for private and corporate donors.

As part of the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability , the Precourt Institute for Energy concentrates the talents of the University on energy research and education, from basic science and technology to policy and business. We disseminate research results and help the University develop energy-literate leaders as part of its educational mission. We work across campus in all seven of Stanford’s schools. Seeking Managing Director, Stanford Center for Sustainability in Southeast Asia:

Seeking exceptional candidates to serve as the Managing Director of the Stanford Center for Sustainabilit in Southeast Asia, a high-impact new research center within the Precourt Institute aimed at developing and implementing long term, holistic solutions for the sustainability of Southeast Asian communities and the envionments on which they depend.

Working in conjunction with the Stanford Center for Sustainability in Southeast Asia faculty Director and reporting directly to the Precourt Institute Director, the Managing Director will lead the development, management, and execution of the Center for Sustainability in Southeast Asia (CSSA). The Stanford Center for Sustainability in Southeast Asia (CSSA) is a new holistic and integrated center that brings together faculty and researchers from all across the Stanford community to work hand-in-hand with key partners and stakeholders from across Southeast Asia and globally. What’s the job and who is Nuru?

Nuru is seeking a multidisciplinary professional with a demonstrated systems thinking, strategic writing, and project management background in international development and impact investing to serve as our Development Systems & Grants Director. This is an internal-facing project management role intentionally designed for a tech-driven operator who thrives on transforming data, donor intelligence, and programmatic knowledge into compelling narratives, strategic insights, and funding opportunities. This is not a lead generation or donor relationship cultivation role. Rather, the Director serves as the architect of Nuru's private and corporate internal fundraising systems, knowledge management processes, and proposal pipeline - we call this “running the internal fundraising machine”. Working closely with the Chief Sustainability Officer, Senior Leadership Team, and a part-time Salesforce Administrator, this role ensures that organizational knowledge is transformed into high-quality proposals, reports, donor profiles, and strategic decision-making tools. The ideal candidate combines deep sectoral expertise with exceptional writing and analytical abilities and possesses a demonstrated track record of designing, managing, and implementing programs that improve rural livelihoods and economic empowerment in geographies relevant to Nuru's mission and vision.

Nuru is a U.S. 501(c)(3) nonprofit with the ability to hire employees globally. Founded in 2008, Nuru is a global collective of locally-led NGO’s working to break cycles of unjust poverty in marginalized communities across the Nuru Collective. We achieve this by helping smallholder farmers transition from subsistence to professionalized farming. While Nuru staff work across separate and locally led organizations in different countries, we are united by a shared vision to expand meaningful choices for the communities we serve. 

A pioneer in remote work, Nuru has been fully remote since 2008. Our team members work from the locations that suit them best, and we remain committed to this flexible, remote-first model. For this role, candidates must be able to maintain regular working overlap with the U.S. Eastern Time.

What you’ll be doing:

● Systems Architecture & Development Operations 

Serve as the architect of Nuru's private and corporate fundraising systems, transforming donor intelligence and organizational knowledge into actionable insights for leadership.
Supervise and prioritize the work of the Salesforce Administrator to ensure Salesforce remains the organization's trusted source of truth.
Design and maintain proposal pipelines, donor profiles, strategic brief sheets, and knowledge management systems that support fundraising effectiveness.
Oversee data governance standards and oversee CRM processes, reporting structures, and operational workflows.
Collaborate closely with the Chief Implementation Officer and Business Development Director to ensure alignment across public and private fundraising efforts.

● Institutional Grants & Lifecycle Strategy

Lead the writing, editing, and collaborative execution of high-quality grant proposals, concept notes, and letters of intent for private and corporate donors. 
Manage tracking systems for private and corporate philanthropy lifecycles, ensuring all compliance milestones, deadlines, and impact reporting deliverables are met with precision.
Convene cross-departmental teams to coordinate action in the development and execution of all private and corporate business development and fundraising. 
Develop donor intelligence profiles and strategic positioning materials for priority funders.
Leverage generative AI and knowledge management systems to accelerate content creation, improve organizational efficiency and preserve institutional memory.

What You’ll Focus On (First 3-6 Months):

● Lead end-to-end proposal development and donor reporting processes for private and corporate opportunities.
● Establish an integrated project management and knowledge management system, including AI enabled workflows, to improve organizational efficiency and institutional memory.
● Develop strategic donor profiles and briefing systems for priority funding prospects.
● Implement a regular cadence for pipeline reviews, reporting, and opportunity tracking.
● Partner with the Salesforce Administrator to review current CRM governance, audit data quality, and strengthen data entry standards.
● Improve cross-functional coordination between programs, MEL, finance, and communications.
● Integrate AI-enabled workflows into proposal development and strengthen institutional knowledge.

What you bring to the team:

● Required Experience

7+ years of professional experience with a global NGO, social enterprise, or impact investing environment.
Solid technical understanding of global nonprofit development and rural livelihoods (e.g. expertise in sectors such as agriculture, food systems, climate resilience, regenerative agriculture, market systems development, agri-SME strengthening, nature-based solutions, and climate finance) with the ability to convert technical programmatic knowledge into compelling donor narratives, strategic positioning, and investment opportunities.
Proven experience leading grant proposal development, donor reporting, and cross-functional projects.
Demonstrated proficiency in utilizing AI productivity tools to optimize workflows, conduct research and draft donor deliverables. 

● Bonus Skills (Please apply even if you don’t check every box!):

Salesforce Certified Administrator credential (backend management and configuration experience, not just end-user experience).
Experience creating and managing organizational knowledge management frameworks.
Working or intermediate proficiency in French.

Who you are:

● Systems Thinker
- You understand how people, processes, and technology interact. You are capable of designing scalable workflows, improving data quality, and transforming information into actionable insights.
● Exceptional Writer and Synthesizer
- You possess superior writing, editing, and storytelling abilities. You can distill complex technical and programmatic information into persuasive proposals, executive briefs, donor reports, and presentations tailored to diverse audiences.
● Project Management
- You manage multiple initiatives simultaneously, balancing priorities, deadlines, and stakeholder expectations. You bring structure and accountability while maintaining flexibility and a collaborative spirit.
● Analytical and Data-Literate
- You are comfortable working with CRM systems, dashboards, and data architectures to organize information and identify trends.
● Cross-Functional Collaborator
- You communicate with clarity and humility, excelling at bringing colleagues across impact activities, finance, MEL, communications, and leadership to advance shared goals. ● Cross-Cultural Aptitude
- You highly respect and eagerly learn from other cultures and demonstrate empathy and effectiveness when working with globally distributed teams.
● Detail-Oriented
- You establish priorities, communicate clearly, maintain rigorous quality standards, and ensure that proposals, reports, and systems are accurate, timely, and compliant.

What Nuru offers you: 

● Culture of Wellbeing:
A 100% remote, flexible work environment that prioritizes personal resiliency and a healthy work/life satisfaction. 
● Commitment to Growth:
Access to professional development, clear paths for career advancement, and a leadership team dedicated to mutual feedback and coaching.

● Competitive Compensation

The Opportunity

We are building an integrated orthopedic and medical device company through the acquisition and combination of businesses across orthopedic distribution, implant manufacturing, surgical instruments, biologics, and technology-enabled surgical solutions.

Our objective is to create a substantial national and international medical device company and prepare it for a future Nasdaq listing.

We are seeking a founding Chief Operating Officer to build the operating structure required to integrate acquired companies, improve their performance, and operate them as one coordinated enterprise. This executive will work directly with the CEO, CFO, and transaction team and will receive a meaningful equity interest in the company.

This is an early-stage, equity-based opportunity. It is not appropriate for a candidate seeking an immediate salary, a narrowly defined role, or an established organization with mature systems already in place.

Responsibilities

The Chief Operating Officer will be responsible for the operating performance and integration of the platform, including:
Leading post-acquisition integration across personnel, systems, supply chain, manufacturing, commercial operations, quality, regulatory compliance, and organizational culture.
Managing the integration of multiple acquired companies concurrently.
Establishing company-wide operating procedures, reporting systems, performance standards, and accountability.
Selecting and implementing appropriate ERP, quality management, financial reporting, and operational systems.
Developing key performance indicators and a formal management reporting process.
Improving profitability, operating margins, working capital management, and organic growth within acquired businesses.
Identifying and implementing cost savings, purchasing efficiencies, manufacturing improvements, and commercial synergies.
Supporting operational due diligence and evaluating the integration requirements of prospective acquisitions.
Advising the leadership team on acquisition sequencing, integration risk, management requirements, and capital needs.
Building and managing the corporate and operating teams required as the company expands.
Preparing the organization to meet the operational, financial reporting, compliance, and governance requirements expected of a public company.

Required Experience

Candidates must have:
Direct, hands-on experience leading post-merger integrations.
A demonstrated record of combining acquired companies, consolidating systems and operations, retaining key personnel, and achieving measurable operating improvements.
Senior operating experience in orthopedics, medical devices, medical technology, or a closely related sector.
Knowledge of medical device distribution, manufacturing, supply chain management, quality systems, regulatory requirements, and commercial relationships.
Experience working with surgeons, hospitals, integrated delivery networks, distributors, manufacturers, or OEM partners.
Prior leadership experience as a Chief Operating Officer, divisional president, general manager, or Vice President/Senior Vice President of Operations.
Full profit-and-loss responsibility or substantial responsibility for operating and financial performance.
The ability to build systems, teams, and processes in an early-stage environment.
The judgment and discipline to manage several operating priorities and acquisition integrations simultaneously.

Experience preparing a medical device or healthcare company for a public offering, institutional investment, or significant corporate transaction is strongly preferred.

Compensation

This position will initially be compensated through equity only. There will be no salary during the first five months while the company completes its initial acquisitions and secures its capital base.

The selected executive will receive a meaningful equity interest appropriate for a founding Chief Operating Officer responsible for building the company’s operating platform. Cash compensation is expected to begin after the company is funded and its initial acquisitions are completed.

Candidates should carefully consider this compensation structure before applying. This opportunity is intended for an experienced executive who is financially able to accept an initial equity-only position and who wants substantial ownership in the business being created.

Final compensation, equity, vesting, responsibilities, and employment terms will be documented in a formal agreement.

Measure and track campaign effectiveness and digital properties

Collaborate with Development and Program staff to write and edit all public-facing content
